title: Taste Bench score (one human reviewer, one pair)
description: Filled in by a human reviewer from the pair's score-form.json and committed as bench/scores/<pair-id>/<github-handle>.json. bench/scripts/validate_scores.py enforces this schema and also rejects reviewer names that name software, timestamps before the blinding commitment or in the future, and duplicate reviews.

github.description: The reviewer's GitHub handle; the score's pull request comes from this account.

submitted_at.description: ISO 8601 with a time zone, e.g. 2026-11-02T14:05:00Z.

other_scores_unseen_while_scoring.description: You did not open any other reviewer's score file or pull request before submitting this one.

task_fit.description: Does the screen do what the brief asks, for the person it describes?

hierarchy.description: Is it clear what matters most, what to read first and what to do next?

mobile_usability.description: At 390 px, is it comfortable to read and operate, not a squeezed desktop?

discoverability.description: Can people find the controls and paths the brief needs without guessing?

density.description: Is the amount of information per screen right for the task: not cramped, not sparse?

coherence.description: Do the parts read as one designed screen rather than assembled pieces?

consistency.description: Are the same things done the same way across the screen and its states?

component_reuse.description: Are repeated elements (buttons, fields, rows, messages) visibly one consistent set?

accessibility.description: Labels, contrast, focus, target size and structure; use the axe counts as one input.

restraint.description: Free of decoration, effects and invented content the task does not need?

regression_risk.description: How likely is it to break or mislead in real use: overflow, broken states, risky actions?

ship_readiness.description: Could this be shipped as it is, with minor fixes at most?

note.description: What you saw that explains the scores.
